accepted_units.title: Convex order as the exact feasibility condition for martingale coupling
accepted_units.why_material: The source identifies a global family of convex test inequalities as both necessary and sufficient for a coupling with the prescribed conditional-barycenter constraint, separating semantic feasibility from any particular construction.
accepted_units.context_note: Necessity is the Jensen direction; sufficiency is developed constructively in the following unit. The extraction preserves the logical statement but damages some order symbols and displayed formulas.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: This criterion depends materially on probability measures on the real line, integrability, convex test functions, and the martingale/barycenter representation.

accepted_units.title: Existence by atomic splitting, ordered approximation, and compactness
accepted_units.why_material: A feasible coupling is built first by recursively allocating the target around source atoms while preserving convex order, then extended to general measures through monotone atomic approximation and a compactness limit.
accepted_units.context_note: This gives a reusable decomposition-plus-limit move rather than merely citing existence. Exact formulas for split measures and order relations should be checked against the PDF.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The construction uses the total order of the real line, atomic approximants, barycenters, weak convergence, and uniform first-moment control.

accepted_units.title: Global optimality forces resistance to finite constraint-preserving competitors
accepted_units.why_material: The variational principle turns a global transport optimum into a full-measure local support property: no finite subconfiguration can be rerouted with the same marginals and conditional barycenters at lower cost.
accepted_units.context_note: The proof uses a null-set versus positive-measure alternative followed by measurable averaging; the brief dual formulation immediately before this span is supporting context, not treated as an additional unit.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Material constraints are equality of both marginals and preservation of the conditional first moment; omitting the barycenter constraint changes the competitor class.

accepted_units.title: Convex potentials convert measure order into pointwise geometry
accepted_units.why_material: Measures are encoded by convex potential functions, making convex order a pointwise comparison and submeasure domination a curvature comparison; an extended order mediates between convex order and ordinary measure domination.
accepted_units.context_note: This representation change supplies the language for shadows, decomposition, and later dual arguments. Superscripts, inequalities, and distributional second-derivative notation are extraction-risk points.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The equivalence relies on one-dimensional absolute-value potentials, equal mass/barycenter where required, and distributional curvature.

accepted_units.title: Shadow as the least feasible target submeasure in convex order
accepted_units.why_material: The shadow is characterized as the convex-order-minimal target submeasure capable of receiving a given source measure, producing a canonical projection under simultaneous feasibility and domination constraints.
accepted_units.context_note: Existence is obtained from an infimum of potentials stabilized by a convex-hull/minimum construction; exact displayed identities are partly damaged but the universal minimality argument is readable.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The construction depends on the potential representation, extended convex order, and one-dimensional convex envelopes.

accepted_units.title: Associativity and continuity of sequential shadows
accepted_units.why_material: The shadow of a sum can be computed sequentially by taking the first shadow and then the shadow of the residual source in the residual target; continuity and atomic approximation extend the recurrence to general measures.
accepted_units.context_note: The result explains why incremental allocations remain globally canonical and supports the prefix construction that follows. Several formula-heavy recurrences require notation-level verification.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Associativity uses target subtraction, extended convex order, and the minimality of shadows; continuity is in weak/first-moment topologies.

accepted_units.title: Canonical coupling from shadows of nested prefixes
accepted_units.why_material: Assigning every member of a nested generating family of source prefixes to its shadow determines a consistent joint measure whose conditional barycenters give the martingale property; finite rerouting excludes the forbidden crossing geometry.
accepted_units.context_note: The construction isolates a choice-free object from compatible partial projections. The term left-curtain and the geometric diagram are source-specific labels/illustrations rather than additional mechanisms.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The canonical prefix family uses the total order on the source line and shadow associativity; an arbitrary multidimensional family need not have the same nesting or uniqueness.

accepted_units.title: Prefix minimality and fiber geometry force uniqueness
accepted_units.why_material: Prefix-shadow minimality identifies the monotone coupling uniquely; for atomless sources, forbidden support patterns restrict conditional fibers to two graphs, and a convex-set half-sum argument turns that restriction into rigidity.
accepted_units.context_note: This combines an order-theoretic uniqueness proof with a geometric support argument. Some theorem symbols and the picture of forbidden configurations are degraded in extraction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The two-graph conclusion uses source continuity and order on the real line; the half-sum argument additionally requires every admissible member considered to have fibers of cardinality at most two.

accepted_units.title: Cost curvature converts a forbidden local rerouting into canonical optimality
accepted_units.why_material: Strict convexity of a derivative of the cost makes the forbidden finite support pattern admit a cheaper constraint-preserving competitor, so the variational principle forces monotonicity and selects the canonical optimizer.
accepted_units.context_note: An alternate proof integrates prefix minimality. The exact sign conventions and derivative formulas are extraction-sensitive and should not be reconstructed from damaged glyphs.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The conclusion depends on differentiability and strict convexity in the stated variable, integrability of the cost, and the one-dimensional ordering that defines the forbidden pattern.

accepted_units.title: Derivative intersection complexity bounds conditional support
accepted_units.why_material: A bound on intersections between a cost derivative and affine functions becomes a bound on the number of points in each conditional support, via the impossibility of an improving local rerouting.
accepted_units.context_note: The argument is a reusable bridge from analytic complexity of a cost to combinatorial sparsity of an optimizer; exact root-count hypotheses are formula-risk material.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: It relies on smoothness, a specified intersection-count condition, martingale linear constraints, and support regularity supplied by the variational principle.

accepted_units.title: Quartic counterexamples stress-test uniqueness and support bounds
accepted_units.why_material: Explicit quartic examples show that uniqueness can fail and that a three-way conditional split can be sharp, preventing the preceding hypotheses from being weakened silently.
accepted_units.context_note: This unit is retained only as a conceptual stress test. Its numerical identities and polynomial formulas are damaged enough that exact verification requires the PDF, and the concrete arithmetic is not generic model-visible mathematics.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The counterexamples depend on the chosen discrete measures, quartic cost, and exact numerical balance relations; they do not establish a general construction outside those hypotheses.

accepted_units.title: Potential gaps canonically decompose transport into irreducible components
accepted_units.why_material: Connected components of the strict gap between source and target potentials determine unique independent transport components plus a static remainder, and global optimality reduces exactly to optimality on each component.
accepted_units.context_note: This decomposition exposes where nontrivial motion is possible before optimization. Component and restriction notation is partially degraded, but the uniqueness and reduction logic remain readable.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The construction relies on one-dimensional potential functions, connected components of an open subset of the line, and disintegration/restriction of measures and couplings.

accepted_units.title: Finite dual certificates compactify to a global certificate
accepted_units.why_material: Finite optimality yields linear-programming dual certificates on every finite subset; normalization and irreducibility provide compatible bounds, and a finite-intersection compactness argument produces global potentials that are then regularized by a convex envelope.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a distinct local-to-global move from the primal variational principle: finite constraints generate a global dual witness. Long inequalities and envelope formulas need source-image verification.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The proof uses finite-dimensional LP duality, irreducibility for bounds and normalization, product compactness, and convex-envelope regularization.

accepted_units.title: Renormalization makes dual potentials integrable and glues componentwise optimality
accepted_units.why_material: Adding and subtracting a convex correction changes dual representatives while leaving their value on every martingale coupling invariant, allowing integrable certificates to be assembled across irreducible components and used for global optimality.
accepted_units.context_note: The move separates representational pathologies of a certificate from its invariant content. Exact integrability inequalities are formula-sensitive.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Invariance relies on the conditional-barycenter identity, while gluing relies on the preceding irreducible decomposition and componentwise dual equality.

accepted_units.title: Density and quantile transfer regularize conditional support
accepted_units.why_material: Lebesgue-density and quantile arguments produce a full-measure set on which points in a conditional support recur jointly over nearby base points with positive mass, bridging fiberwise support statements to configurations usable by a finite variation.
accepted_units.context_note: This technical bridge is material because arbitrary conditional kernels are defined only almost everywhere. Several interval and quantile formulas are extraction-risk points.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The construction uses regular conditional probabilities on the real line, order-based quantiles, density differentiation, and local neighborhoods in the base space.

accepted_units.title: Perturbing and spreading a finite variation contradicts global optimality
accepted_units.why_material: A finite improving variation is perturbed across nearby regular fibers while preserving both marginal and barycenter constraints, then averaged so its positive part is dominated by the original plan, yielding an admissible global competitor and a contradiction.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a constructive proof of the variational principle distinct from the earlier descriptive proof route. The source notes that this real-line construction does not readily extend to general product spaces.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: It depends on continuity of the cost, one-dimensional regular support transfer, solvability of the local linear constraints, and domination after averaging.

ecosystem_findings.summary: The source internally links convex feasibility tests, pointwise potential geometry, canonical minimal submeasures, local cost separation, support bounds, and dual certificates. This reinforces the routed lens only; novelty relative to the existing corpus was not inspected.

Constraint-preserving finite variations provide a primal local test, while finite LP certificates compactify and renormalize into global dual witnesses. The finding is source-internal support, not a corpus-level novelty claim.

Potential functions, minimal shadows, nested prefixes, and connected potential-gap components turn measure order and transport constraints into geometric objects that can be constructed and decomposed. No cross-corpus comparison was performed.

The martingale barycenter condition acts simultaneously as a feasibility invariant, a coupling constraint, and a kernel-level support condition. The evidence is for a one-step two-marginal setting and should not be generalized to arbitrary stochastic processes.
